extracted.intended_audience: federal judges and patent litigators (especially practitioners in the District of Delaware)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive case-management rules and best practices for handling civil patent litigation (scheduling, discovery, claim construction, motions practice, pretrial and trial logistics), particularly for cases assigned to Judge Leonard P. Stark in the District of Delaware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss known points of contention
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss known points of contention (e.g., prosecution bar, levels of confidentiality, access by in-house lawyers) and, if applicable, convey the court’s general perspective on such issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify areas likely to produce disputes and the court’s general view to facilitate meet-and-confer and CMC discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willfulness issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss special issues related to willfulness (if asserted), including timing of the assertion of the claim, timing of the reliance on any opinion of counsel, possibility of bifurcation, and possibility of disqualification of counsel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider bifurcating willfulness and early briefing on opinions of counsel; anticipate potential counsel conflicts or disqualification topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative dispute resolution (ADR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss alternative dispute resolution (ADR): usefulness, timing, mediation, arbitration, or other form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate ADR early and schedule opportunities for mediation/arbitration where useful to case resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic discovery scope & limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss electronic discovery and consider limitations on discovery: format(s) for production of electronic discovery; limits on the scope of electronic discovery; source code – how will it be produced?; limits on the number of custodians; number of total hours for fact witnesses or number of depositions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set concrete ESI production formats, custodian limits, and source-code protocols at CMC to avoid disputes and overbroad fishing expeditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contention disclosures and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss contention disclosures and schedule therefor: in patent local rule jurisdictions, discuss whether variance from the standard disclosure timelines is appropriate; in jurisdictions without patent local rules, discuss whether the parties should exchange infringement, invalidity, unenforceability, and damages contentions and the appropriate schedule for such disclosures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a timeline for exchange of contentions (infringement, invalidity, damages, unenforceability) or explain deviations from local patent rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedures for claim construction and dispositive motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set timing and procedures for claim construction and dispositive motions: determine timing of summary judgment relative to claim construction; if not addressed by local rule, set a schedule for exchanges of claim terms, proposed constructions, and supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate Markman schedule with summary judgment practice; set explicit deadlines for term exchanges and evidence to avoid late surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorials for technology/terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether a tutorial would be appropriate: How conducted: By counsel? By experts? Submissions (e.g., DVDs)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the court will accept tutorial presentations, identify presenters, and set format and submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winnowing patents/claims and claim-term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the number of patents and patent claims that would be tried and possible ways of winnowing; discuss limits on the number of claim terms submitted for construction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explanation of the significance of each disputed term (e.g., effect on infringement/validity) and ask parties to rank disputed terms by significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction hearing logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss claim construction hearing logistics: identify disputed subsidiary factual issues; discuss whether live witnesses should be called
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage use of graphics, animations, and other visual displays to aid in understanding the technology and disputed claim terms; schedule a pre-claim-construction conference to finalize logistics after positions have crystallized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary judgment dependence on claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether any summary judgment issues depend on claim construction or can otherwise be resolved with little or no discovery, including: dispute about structure/function of accused products; any claim term that, once decided, will compel infringement or noninfringement; territorial issues; any claims or defenses purely legal in nature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If purely legal issues exist, consider first-track and second-track schedules for summary judgment to speed resolution (see Chapter 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on summary judgment motions and briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss whether any limits on the number of summary judgment motions (or number of pages of briefing) should be imposed or modified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may set caps on number and length of motions to keep briefing manageable and equitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on prior art references
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limits on prior art references
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set caps and narrowing procedures for prior art references to focus invalidity issues and reduce discovery burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daubert and in limine motion scheduling and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss issues related to Daubert and in limine motions: schedule Daubert motions well in advance of pretrial conference, for example concurrently with summary judgment; discuss scope of in limine motion practice and advise parties that the court will not consider dispositive motions disguised as in limine motions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate expert challenge schedule with dispositive motions; be vigilant against procedurally improper in limine filings attempting to decide dispositive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages contentions and expedited damages discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages – discuss whether it would be appropriate to require damages contentions and/or an expedited damages discovery schedule, or to take other steps to facilitate the early resolution of challenges to damages-related theories or expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider requiring early damages models and targeted discovery to resolve damages disputes sooner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core technical documents identification
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the core technical documents?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify documents essential for understanding accused products early to focus document discovery and reduce overproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email discovery: custodians and search methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Does any party intend to request production of electronic mail? If so, why? How many custodians should be searched? What methods will be used to search for electronic documents (e.g., key word searches, predictive coding)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require parties to justify e-mail production scope and specify search protocols (keywords, TAR/predictive coding) to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatory adequacy and meaningful responses
rubrics_metrics.description: How can the Court best assist the parties to provide meaningful interrogatory responses to avoid discovery disputes over the adequacy of such responses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage detailed, substantive interrogatory answers; adequacy judged by level of detail provided—more detail begets more detail in return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source code production protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: If source code is going to be produced, when, where, and how will it be made available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set explicit production protocol for source code (format, review site, protective order handling) to protect confidentiality and reduce later disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Super-early limited claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the 1 or 2 most important claim terms requiring construction? Should the Court consider a “super-early” limited claim construction hearing on those most important terms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a narrow early Markman on dispositive terms to streamline the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing the case
rubrics_metrics.description: At what point(s) in the case will it be appropriate to limit/reduce the number of accused devices/functionalities, asserted patents, asserted claims, invalidity defenses (including obviousness combinations), and prior art references? Are there products not colorably different that may be added? Should damages or any other portion of the case be bifurcated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court is highly receptive to reasonable proposals to reduce scope at appropriate stages to improve efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related cases coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: What related cases are pending, in any Court, and what is their filing date and current status? Does Plaintiff plan to file additional related cases and, if so, on what schedule and how should that plan affect how this case will proceed? Has any patent-in-suit been litigated before and how soon is Plaintiff willing to produce the results of any such litigation, including settlement agreements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate schedules for related cases and ensure relevant prior litigation materials are produced promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and initial damages information
rubrics_metrics.description: What initial revenue/sales information does Plaintiff need to assess the value of the case and how soon is Defendant willing to produce such information? What type of relief is Plaintiff seeking: lost profits, reasonable royalties, injunction, and/or any other form of relief? What does Plaintiff contend is the 'smallest saleable unit'? Has the patent been licensed or offered for any license and how soon is Plaintiff willing to produce licensing information?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require early exchange of basic financial and licensing information to facilitate damages analysis and possible narrowing or settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and deadlines for pleadings and accused products
rubrics_metrics.description: What will be the deadline for proposed amendments to the pleadings, including adding allegations of indirect and/or willful infringement as well as inequitable conduct? What will be the deadline for adding or altering the accused devices/functionalities, asserted claims, and prior art?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set firm amendment deadlines to avoid late-expanding claims or accused products that disrupt case schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation of contentions and expert declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Will expert declarations/affidavits be permitted to be filed with case-dispositive and other motions, without other parties’ agreement or leave of the Court? What will be the deadline for supplementing infringement, invalidity, damages, and other contentions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify supplementation rules and whether additional expert material may be filed with dispositive motions to prevent surprise and ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective order tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any reasons this case requires provisions that are not typical of the protective order generally entered in this Court’s patent cases?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If atypical protections required (e.g., heightened confidentiality tiers), identify them and propose tailored protective order language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to dismiss/transfer/stay handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Have any motions to dismiss/transfer/stay been filed and/or does any party anticipate filing such a motion? Will the parties consent to magistrate judge jurisdiction at least for the limited purpose of resolving these motions? Should discovery and other exchanges of information be stayed during pendency of these motions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide early whether to stay discovery while threshold motions are pending and consider consenting to magistrate jurisdiction for speedier resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early summary judgment motion considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any motions that are potentially fully case dispositive—or that would be dispositive of such a significant portion of the case that its resolution would greatly enhance the likelihood of a cost-effective pre-trial disposition—and that the parties agree the Court should hear early? If the Court is to hear any early summary judgment motion, which, if any, other parts of the case should be stayed? If the Court is to hear any early summary judgment motion, what is the moving party going to give up (e.g., the opportunity to file a motion on the same subject matter later in the case)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh benefits of early dispositive motions against potential prejudice and define what rights the movant waives by seeking early resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery teleconference procedures and letter practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery motion procedures: parties must submit a joint, non-argumentative letter requesting a discovery teleconference that lists the disputes; the party seeking relief files a three-page letter outlining issues and position not less than 48 hours before the conference; opposing letter of up to three pages may be filed not less than 24 hours prior; submit two courtesy copies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict page limits and a structured joint-letter meet-and-confer process are required before the court will schedule discovery teleconferences; motions filed without complying will be denied without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to amend/strike letter-format procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend or to strike shall not be accompanied by an opening brief but by a letter not to exceed three pages describing the basis and attaching the proposed amended pleading (with blackline); responses limited to five pages and reply to two pages, followed by a letter requesting a teleconference
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form letter practice replaces full briefing at the initial stage to streamline disposition of amendment/strike requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order and CMC attendance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall meet and confer, jointly file the Checklist and a proposed scheduling order within thirty (30) days of order; the Case Management Conference will be held with Judge Stark and/or Judge Burke and each party must be represented by Lead Counsel and Delaware Counsel prepared to discuss each matter on the Checklist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect in-person discussion, good-faith meet-and-confer, and readiness to explain any topic deemed inappropriate or premature to discuss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery modifications specific to Judge Stark's procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery modifications include no requirement to call chambers to request a discovery teleconference (use joint letter), no requirement to submit copies of sealed documents within an hour of filing, and requirement to submit two courtesy copies of discovery letters and attachments; teleconferences limited to ~30-45 minutes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the streamlined letter practice and respect teleconference time limits to obtain judicial attention to disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Standards and staged exchange of contentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent agreement, scheduling will include dates for staged exchange: Plaintiff to identify accused products, damages model, and produce file history; Defendant to produce core technical documents and sales figures; Plaintiff to produce initial claim chart; Defendant to produce initial invalidity contentions; Plaintiff final infringement contentions; Defendant final invalidity contentions; date for final supplementation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the court’s baseline expectations (mirror Judge Robinson’s SLR Order) for contentions and cores; parties may agree to deviate but scheduling order will include these dates by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markman rulings and Markman hearing preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspirational goal of issuing all Markman rulings within 60 days after a Markman hearing; preference for a single Markman hearing but flexible; parties should be prepared to discuss earlier construction of certain terms where efficient
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court will advise if it cannot meet the 60-day goal; generally skeptical that 'plain and ordinary meaning' resolves material disputes and will usually expect proposed constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and combined caps for summary judgment and Daubert briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file as many summary judgment and Daubert motions as they wish, subject to side limits: no more than 50 pages of combined opening briefs, 50 pages of combined answering briefs, and 20 pages of combined reply briefs per side. The Court expects no more than 250 total pages of briefing on all case-dispositive and Daubert motions across consolidated schedules. Argument typically limited to ~45 minutes per side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict combined-page caps preserve judicial resources; parties must coordinate their motions to stay within caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretrial order trial length and time accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: When estimating anticipated length of trial, parties must provide days and a specific number of hours for trial presentations; counsel should assume they will be charged time for opening statements, witness examination (including playing or reading deposition testimony), closing arguments, arguing objections (including mornings before trial), and arguing motions; typical trial day: 5.5–6.5 hours (jury) and 6–7 hours (bench)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide granular hour estimates and be aware which trial activities are charged vs. not charged (usually not charged: jury selection, opening/final jury instructions, arguments regarding jury instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to expert testimony scope at trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel need to indicate whether, with respect to objections to expert testimony as being beyond the scope of previous expert disclosures, they request that the Court rule on such objections at trial or defer ruling until post-trial motions (with costs of new trial charged to the party whose conduct necessitates a new trial)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to have in-trial rulings or defer to post-trial; consequences for a new trial's cost allocation should be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 50 (JMOL) procedure preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to motions for judgment as a matter of law pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 50, counsel need to indicate whether they request such motions: (i) be made at sidebar while the jury remains in the courtroom, (ii) be made immediately at the appropriate point during trial, and (iii) be supplemented in writing (and, if so, when)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify preferred timing and whether written supplementation will occur to give the Court appropriate notice and manage courtroom time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretrial conference time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Pretrial conferences will generally be limited to two (2) hours or less
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be focused and prioritize issues for the limited pretrial conference time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury instructions and voir dire file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a case is to be tried to a jury, the parties must provide courtesy copies of proposed voir dire, preliminary and final jury instructions, and special verdict forms as computer files in WordPerfect or Microsoft Word
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send courtesy digital copies (email to chambers staff) in specified formats to facilitate drafting and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-verdict joint status report and judgment entry
rubrics_metrics.description: After the jury returns a verdict, the Court will generally order preparation of a joint status report indicating how the parties believe the case should proceed, including whether additional briefing or in-court proceedings are required; the report should identify post-trial motions and be accompanied by a proposed order to enter judgment on the verdict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet and confer before filing to present a unified plan and proposed judgment entry to streamline post-verdict proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-trial motions briefing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered, post-trial briefing is according to Local Rules regardless of how many motions are filed: each side may file a maximum total of 20 pages of opening briefing, 20 pages of answering briefing, and 10 pages of reply briefing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local Rule page limits apply cumulatively to post-trial briefing to prevent excessive papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 26 initial disclosures and ESI default standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures shall be made within five (5) days of the date of the Revised Patent Form Scheduling Order; parties are to review and adhere to the Court’s Default Standard for Discovery, Including Discovery of Electronically Stored Information (ESI)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply promptly with initial disclosures and the Court’s ESI Default Standards to avoid discovery disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective order sealing/redaction and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed protective order must include a paragraph notifying parties that another court may find information relevant and subject to disclosure; motions to seal/redact transcripts require prompt filing and demonstration of good cause and specific serious injury if disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking sealing/redaction, attach highlighted transcript and proposed redacted version and explain narrowly tailored reasons for sealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy copies requirement for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than discovery matters and the final pretrial order, the parties shall provide two (2) courtesy copies of all briefs and one (1) courtesy copy of any other document filed in support of any briefs (appendices, exhibits, declarations, affidavits, etc.), including sealed papers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely physical courtesy copies per the Court’s instructions to assist judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery limitations and timing (Local Rule 26.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered, the limitations on discovery set forth in Local Rule 26.1 shall be strictly observed, including scheduling for discovery cut-off, document production substantially complete by set date, limits on requests for admission and interrogatories, and deposition hour limits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe numerical and timing limits in Local Rule 26.1; interrogatory adequacy judged by level of detail; deposition hours/location rules apply with limited exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories and contention interrogatories practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum number of interrogatories (including contention interrogatories) are permitted for each side; the Court encourages serving and responding to contention interrogatories early in the case; in absence of agreement, contention interrogatories shall first be addressed by the party with the burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should provide detailed contention answers early; adequacy judged by level of detail—more detail justifies more detail in response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions: total hours and location rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each side is limited to a total number of hours of taking testimony by deposition upon oral examination; depositions of party representatives should ordinarily be taken within the district unless exception ordered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and enforce deposition hour caps to control cost; expect local deposition location rules to apply.
